title: Cleopatra lived closer to the iPhone than to the pyramids
script: Cleopatra lived closer to the iPhone than to the pyramids. The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC. Cleopatra died in 30 BC, about 2,500 years later. The first iPhone came out just over 2,000 years after her.
description: Ancient Egypt was ancient even to Cleopatra.

title: Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire
script: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire. Teaching at Oxford began around 1096. The Aztecs founded their capital, Tenochtitlan, in 1325. By then, Oxford students had been sitting through lectures for over two centuries.

title: Mammoths were alive when the pyramids were built
script: Mammoths were still alive when the pyramids were built. A small group survived on Wrangel Island, off the coast of Siberia, until about 4,000 years ago. By then, the Great Pyramid was already centuries old.
description: The last mammoths outlived the pyramid builders' early days.

title: Napoleon wasn't actually short
script: Napoleon wasn't short. He was about 1.69 meters tall, average for a Frenchman of his time. The myth came from mixing up French and English inches, plus British cartoons that drew him as a tiny, angry man.
description: The most successful smear campaign in history.

title: Vikings never wore horned helmets
script: Vikings never wore horned helmets. There's zero evidence they did. The look was invented in 1876 by a costume designer for Wagner's opera, The Ring of the Nibelung. One stage outfit fooled the world for 150 years.

title: Ancient Rome taxed urine
script: Ancient Rome taxed urine. Public toilets sold it to laundries and tanners, because the ammonia cleaned clothes and softened leather. Emperor Vespasian taxed the trade, and when his son complained, he replied: money doesn't stink.
description: Where the phrase 'money doesn't stink' comes from.

title: A war once lasted under 45 minutes
script: A war once lasted under 45 minutes. In 1896, Britain and Zanzibar went to war. British ships shelled the sultan's palace, and it was all over in less time than a football half.

title: In 1582, ten days vanished
script: In 1582, ten days simply vanished. To fix the calendar, Pope Gregory the Thirteenth ordered that October 4th be followed by October 15th. People went to sleep on a Thursday and woke up on a Friday, ten days later.
description: How the Gregorian calendar deleted ten days.

title: Cleopatra wasn't Egyptian
script: Cleopatra wasn't Egyptian. Her family, the Ptolemies, were Macedonian Greeks who ruled Egypt for nearly 300 years. Cleopatra was reportedly the first in her family to actually learn the Egyptian language.

title: The Eiffel Tower was supposed to be torn down
script: The Eiffel Tower was supposed to be torn down. It was built for the 1889 World's Fair with a permit for just 20 years. It survived because it turned out to be the perfect giant radio antenna.

title: The lighter was invented before the match
script: The lighter was invented before the match. Johann Döbereiner built his lighter in 1823. The friction match only arrived in 1826, when a chemist named John Walker noticed a coated stick catch fire as he scraped it.

title: Tug of war was an Olympic sport
script: Tug of war used to be an Olympic sport. It was part of the Games from 1900 to 1920. Great Britain won the most medals, and in 1908, all three medal teams were British police officers.

title: World War One was fought between cousins
script: World War One was fought between cousins. King George the Fifth of Britain, Kaiser Wilhelm the Second of Germany, and Tsar Nicholas the Second of Russia were all related. Queen Victoria was grandmother to two of them.
description: The most dysfunctional family in Europe.

title: The fax machine is older than the telephone
script: The fax machine is older than the telephone. Alexander Bain patented a way to send images over telegraph wires in 1843. Alexander Graham Bell's telephone came 33 years later, in 1876.

title: Nintendo is 137 years old
script: Nintendo is 137 years old. It was founded in 1889, making handmade playing cards. Before video games, it also tried a taxi company, instant rice, and even a chain of love hotels.
